jobs.title: Senior Corporate Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description
We are seeking a dynamic and results-oriented   Senior Corporate Strategy Manager   to join our team at Advance Auto Parts. The primary purpose of the role is to support the development and execution of the company’s growth and performance improvement strategy. This position   will lead   high-impact projects across multiple areas, including mergers & acquisitions (M&A), market expansion, competitive analysis, and long-term corporate strategy. This is a high visibility role, with frequent exposure to executives across the enterprise, including the CEO.

A successful candidate for this role thrives in a fast-paced environment and excels at breaking down ambiguous problems into structured, actionable insights. They   demonstrate   curiosity by asking thoughtful questions and have a natural ability to frame complex business challenges. This person is a self-starter who can independently   identify   the right analysis needed, navigate limited or incomplete data, and dig deep to uncover meaningful trends. They are comfortable working without defined ownership of specific business units, juggle multiple projects seamlessly, and are resilient in the face of uncertainty. They embrace the iterative process of learning from mistakes and refining their approach to deliver valuable insights.   Above all, they   are skilled at deriving actionable business recommendations from data and effectively communicating findings across all levels of the organization.

What will you do?

- Corporate Development:   Lead or support due diligence, financial analysis, and   integration   activities for mergers, acquisitions, partnerships, and other strategic investments. Work with internal teams to define strategic rationale in alignment with overall corporate strategy. Evaluate potential targets, create investment   memo , develop valuation models, and present recommendations to executive leaders and business owners.

- Cross-functional collaboration:   Build support and buy-in necessary for the successful execution of our strategic priorities. Partner with Transformation team and business leaders in support of strategic initiatives to ensure alignment to and delivery of strategic priorities. Maintain   comprehensive   understanding of the enterprise and functional areas. Be able to talk to explain business insights to all   level   of the business = including why and how the analysis was done, what does the data   say   about the topic at hand, and recommendations on how to move forward

- Market and Competitive Analysis:   Independently conduct in-depth market research and competitive intelligence and effectively synthesize to build   a common understanding   of our environment and provide actionable insights and recommendations. Analyze industry trends, macroeconomic environment, customer behavior, and competitor strategies to help shape strategic decision-making.

- Strategy development:   Use problem-solving skillset to   assist   in the creation of multi-year strategic plans to support corporate   objectives   and growth. Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to   identify   and evaluate new opportunities and develop strategic initiatives as part of our strategic business planning process.

- Analytical Problem Solving:   Approach open-ended questions with a structured, hypothesis-driven mindset. Frame ambiguous business challenges, ask the right questions, and define the critical analyses needed to address them. Distill large, complex, and raw datasets into clear trends and actionable insights that drive business decisions.

Qualifications:

- Understands the fundamentals of financial performance (e.g., P&L drivers), collaborates effectively with finance partners, and knows when and how to apply statistical modeling or advanced analytical tools to test hypotheses.

- Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to develop and manage relationships with cross-functional stakeholders

- Strong understanding of corporate finance, financial modelling, and valuation techniques

- Ability to build and   maintain   financial models to evaluate potential business opportunities, including investments, acquisitions, and joint ventures

- Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and strategic thinking ability, including the ability to frame ambiguous problems, structure analyses to test hypotheses, take the lead on the analysis, and formulate specific recommendations for action

- Strong written and presentation skills to   facilitate   decision making and drive action

- Adept at explaining not just the outcomes of analyses but also the 'why' and 'how,' ensuring alignment and understanding across all stakeholders, from executives to frontline teams.

- Knowledge of retail, distribution, and / or automotive aftermarket industry

- Proficiency   in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel and PowerPoint. Familiarity with data analysis tools (SQL) is a plus.

Certifications, Experience, and Education:

- Experience : Minimum of 6 years of experience in corporate development, investment banking ,   management consulting ,   corporate   strategy   or related field, ideally within a retail or consumer-focused organization

- Education :   Bachelor’s degree in Busine ss Administration , Finance, Economics, or other relevant fields. MBA or relevant graduate degree preferred. Finance and consulting background preferred.

Location & Work Availability:

This position is Hybrid (4 days in office, 1 day remote), based at our corporate headquarters in Raleigh, North Carolina.

Benefits Summary:

We believe in supporting our Team Members and those they love through comprehensive health & wellness benefits. Learn more here:   https://jobs.advanceautoparts.com/us/en/benefits

Company Overview:

Advance Auto Parts, Inc. is a leading automotive aftermarket parts provider that serves both professional   installer   and do-it-yourself customers. As of January 3, 2026, Advance   operated   4,305 stores primarily within the United States, with   additional   locations in Canada, Puerto   Rico   and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The Company also served 809 independently owned Carquest branded stores across these locations in addition to Mexico and various Caribbean islands.   Additional   information about Advance, including employment opportunities, customer services, and online shopping for parts, accessories and other offerings can be found at   www.AdvanceAutoParts.com .

Job Description
Manager, Corporate Finance & FP&A
Location - Hyderabad, India
Job Summary
We are seeking a highly motivated, strategic, and results-oriented Manager, Corporate Finance & FP&A to lead enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, performance reporting, and strategic financial analysis. This role will own critical planning processes including the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), Strategic Business Plan (SBP), quarterly forecasts, and executive reporting while providing leadership for integrated 3-statement financial modelling.
The role serves as a key finance partner to executive leadership and plays a pivotal role in quarterly Board of Directors (BoD) reporting, earnings call preparation, and investor-related financial analysis. The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise, executive communication skills, and leadership capabilities to drive business performance, enhance forecasting accuracy, and support strategic decision-making.
This position requires a proven leader who can influence across a matrixed organization, develop high-performing teams, and drive continuous improvements in financial planning and reporting processes.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead enterprise-wide planning processes including AOP, SBP, long-range planning, and quarterly forecasts.
- Develop accurate financial forecasts, scenario analyses, and strategic recommendations to support business objectives.
- Own and enhance integrated Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow forecasting models.
- Drive monthly, quarterly, and annual financial performance reviews, highlighting key trends, risks, opportunities, and business drivers.
- Prepare executive presentations, Board materials, KPI dashboards, and financial narratives for leadership reviews.
- Partner closely with business leaders, Accounting, Investor Relations, Operations, and Corporate Finance teams to support strategic initiatives and business decision-making.
- Lead enterprise-wide Risk & Opportunities assessments and develop mitigation strategies to improve forecast accuracy.
- Identify opportunities to improve profitability, productivity, cash flow, and operational performance through data-driven insights.
- Drive FP&A transformation initiatives, including automation, reporting enhancements, driver-based forecasting, and process standardization.
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of 7-8 finance professionals, fostering a high-performance and collaborative culture.

Qualifications
- Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; CPA, CA, or CFA preferred.
- 11+ years of progressive experience in Corporate Finance, FP&A, Strategic Finance, or related disciplines.
- Strong expertise in financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, variance analysis, and integrated 3-statement financial modelling.
- Proven experience supporting executive leadership, Board of Directors reporting, and earnings-related financial analysis.
- Demonstrated ability to translate complex financial data into executive-level insights and recommendations.
- Strong leadership, stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills.
- Experience operating in a large, matrixed, and fast-paced organization.

Preferred Technical Skills
- Hyperion Planning & Budgeting Cloud Service (PBCS)
- Oracle ERP and financial systems
- Advanced Excel financial modelling
- Financial reporting, analytics, and visualization tools

Why Join Us:
- Strategic Impact: You will own the income statement and 3-statement modeling processes, driving financial excellence and business insights.
- Process Transformation: You will contribute to modernizing our financial planning processes, implementing driver-based forecasting, and improving financial reporting and analysis
- Leadership Exposure: Your work will directly impact key deliverables presented to senior leadership, board of directors, and investors.
- Professional Growth: You will lead and develop a team of high-performing financial analysts, while gaining deep exposure to corporate strategy and financial planning.

The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and requires the ability to network with nearby stores, Hubs, pdq and external suppliers for order fulfillment. The role owns responsibility for maintaining Hub company standards.  This position is full time. Position may require MVR certification, and should complete all training materials and attend all store meetings.

- Inventory accuracy and functions as it relates to the parts department and HUB inventory to include- Onhand accuracy of inventory, shrink results, Cycle Counts, Outages, Planograms, Maxi changes, Price Changes, Front & Face, Truck lead
- Manage and comply with all Hub records and all paperwork policies and procedures
- Urgently Communicate any risks or concerns regarding order fulfillment or shipments to the appropriate store leader(s)

Secondary Responsibilities

- Assist with cores and defects

- Friendly communication
- Ability to locate and stock parts

- Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
- Ability to execute and train inventory systems and store equipment
- High attention to detail

jobs.description:
Job Description
The Sr. Director, Compensation is responsible for the enterprise-wide strategy, design, governance, and execution of Advance’s compensation and recognition programs across Corporate, Field, Supply Chain, and shared services functions. This role serves as the organization’s senior compensation leader, overseeing base pay, short-term and long-term incentives, sales and field incentive plans, and enterprise recognition programs.
The Sr. Director partners closely with executive leadership, HR Business Partners, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and Operations leaders to ensure compensation and recognition programs drive business performance, attract and retain high-performing talent, reinforce company culture, and support Advance’s Total Rewards philosophy. This role develops and executes long-term compensation strategies, leads complex incentive plan design initiatives, and provides strategic counsel on workforce, organizational, and pay-related decisions.

As a key member of the Total Rewards leadership team, the Sr. Director provides leadership through Senior Managers, and specialized compensation professionals while ensuring governance, compliance, market competitiveness, and operational excellence across all compensation and recognition programs.

What will you do?
Enterprise Compensation Strategy
- Develop and gain executive leadership alignment on annual and multi-year compensation and recognition strategies that support organizational growth, workforce planning, and business objectives.

- Establish an integrated compensation philosophy and governance framework across Corporate, Field, and Operations organizations.

- Monitor external trends, regulatory developments, economic factors, and competitive practices to ensure programs remain market competitive and strategically aligned.

- Translate business strategies into innovative compensation solutions that balance performance, affordability, retention, and talent attraction.

Corporate and Field Compensation Leadership
- Provide enterprise leadership for all compensation programs, including corporate, field, retail, distribution centers, sales, and operational populations.

- Oversee compensation structures, pay ranges, job architecture, career frameworks, premium pay programs, geographic differentials, and market pricing methodologies.

- Ensure internal equity and external competitiveness through ongoing evaluation of compensation programs and market benchmarking.

- Lead annual merit, market adjustment, and compensation planning processes.

Incentive Design and Performance Programs
- Own the strategy, design, governance, and effectiveness of all incentive programs across the enterprise.

- Partner with executive, operational, finance, legal, and HR leaders to develop and model:

- Annual incentive plans

- Sales and commission plans

- Operations incentive programs

- Store and field bonus programs

- Retention and special incentive arrangements

- Long-term incentive programs

- Evaluate plan effectiveness through financial modeling, ROI analysis, productivity measures, and performance outcomes.

- Ensure incentive designs support company strategy, reinforce accountability, and drive desired business results.

Enterprise Recognition Strategy
- Lead the strategy, design, governance, and administration of enterprise-wide recognition programs.

- Ensure recognition programs reinforce organizational culture, values, engagement, and retention objectives.

- Evaluate program effectiveness through participation, engagement, retention, and productivity metrics.

- Identify opportunities for modernization, digitalization, and expansion of recognition capabilities across the organization.

Executive and Strategic Compensation Consulting
- Serve as senior advisor to executives and HR leaders on complex compensation matters.

- Provide thought leadership and guidance on organizational design, workforce planning, acquisitions, restructuring activities, and leadership reward strategies.

- Support succession planning and critical talent retention strategies through innovative compensation solutions.

Analytics, Governance, and Compliance
- Establish enterprise compensation, governance practices, policies, and controls.

- Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, and local compensation regulations.

- Lead compensation analytics, workforce insights, and KPI reporting for executive leadership.

- Utilize advanced analytics to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and strategic workforce implications.

- Oversee compensation-related audits and governance reviews.

Program Administration and Operational Excellence
- Partner closely with Compensation Administration, HR Technology, Payroll, and Finance teams to ensure accurate execution of compensation and recognition programs.

- Ensure the integrity of compensation processes, systems, and data.

- Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness and user experience.

- Oversee vendor relationships and external consulting partnerships supporting compensation and recognition programs.

Leadership
- Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of compensation and recognition professionals.

- Build organizational capability across the HR function through education, tools, and consultation.

- Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

- Provide leadership through Managers and functional experts to ensure successful execution of enterprise priorities.

Qualifications
- Demonstrated experience leading compensation functions across both Corporate and Field organizations.

- Significant experience designing and administering incentive compensation programs.

- Experience supporting executive leadership and senior business stakeholders.

- Deep expertise in compensation strategy, job architecture, market pricing, sales compensation, incentive design, and recognition programs.

- Proven ability to design and implement enterprise-wide compensation programs in a complex, multi-location environment.

- Demonstrated experience partnering with senior executives and influencing business decisions.

- Strong financial acumen with expertise in compensation modeling, budgeting, forecasting, and ROI analysis.

- Experience leading large-scale compensation transformations and change management initiatives.

- Demonstrated success leading teams and developing leaders.

- Exceptional analytical, communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

- Ability to balance strategic vision with operational execution.

- Workday experience is strongly preferred.

- Experience working with a Fortune 300 or similarly complex organization preferred.

Certifications, Experience, and Education:
- Certifications :

- CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) preferred.

- GRP, CSCP, or other relevant Total Rewards certifications are preferred.

- Experience : 15+ years of progressive experience in compensation and/or Total Rewards with at least 5+ years in leadership; and

- Education : Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required; Master’s degree preferred; or equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

Location & Work Availability:
This position is Hybrid (4 days in office, 1 day remote), based at our corporate headquarters in Raleigh, North Carolina.

jobs.description:
Job Description
This team member must be located in the northeast region of the US.
The Senior Human Resources Manager is a strategic business partner to the Regional Vice President and regional leadership team, translating business priorities into an integrated people strategy. The role shapes and executes the region’s talent agenda through workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, leadership capability, succession planning, talent acquisition, engagement, and change leadership. The position uses business and workforce insights to anticipate capability needs, strengthen leadership pipelines, improve organizational performance, and build an inclusive culture that attracts, develops, and retains high-performing talent. Employee relations, policy interpretation, and compliance remain important accountabilities, but are managed within a broader strategic HR portfolio and with an emphasis on prevention, leader capability, appropriate escalation, and sustainable solutions.
Role Scope
The Senior Human Resources Manager partners with the Regional Vice President and senior field leaders to influence business and people decisions across the region. The role operates as a trusted advisor, challenges assumptions constructively, connects enterprise HR capabilities to field priorities, and balances near-term execution with longer-term workforce and organizational needs.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Strategic HR Partnership and Business Acumen
• Build and execute a multi-year people strategy aligned to regional business objectives, operating priorities, customer needs, and enterprise HR direction.
• Use business, financial, workforce, and talent data to identify risks, root causes, and opportunities; translate insights into clear priorities, measures, and action plans.
• Advise the Regional Vice President and leadership team on organizational capability, leadership effectiveness, workforce investments, and the people implications of business decisions.
• Facilitate disciplined operating rhythms for talent, organization, culture, and workforce priorities, with clear ownership and follow-through.
Talent Planning and Succession
• Lead the region’s talent planning and calibration process, ensuring consistent, fact-based assessment of performance, potential, readiness, mobility, retention risk, and development needs.
• Identify critical roles and capabilities, evaluate bench strength, and maintain actionable succession plans that include, ready-now and ready-soon successors, and longer-term pipeline options.
• Partner with leaders to create differentiated development, exposure, retention, and movement plans for key talent while reinforcing that every team member receives meaningful coaching and development.
• Integrate succession insights with workforce planning, organizational design, talent acquisition, and leadership development decisions.
• Monitor succession depth, internal movement, readiness progress, talent risk, and development-plan execution; address gaps with leaders and HR partners.
Workforce Planning and Organizational Effectiveness
• Lead strategic workforce planning to assess current and future headcount, skills, leadership capacity, location needs, and organizational capability against the business plan.
• Anticipate the talent and change implications of growth, new initiatives, and competitive intrusion; develop practical transition and capability plans.
• Lead change management strategies that build awareness, understanding, commitment, adoption, and sustained accountability.
Talent Acquisition
•  Partner with Talent Acquisition and field leaders to define success profiles, sourcing strategies, selection approaches, diverse pipelines, hiring priorities, and service expectations.
• Improve quality, speed, and sustainability of hiring by strengthening workforce forecasting, leader readiness, interview discipline, candidate experience, and onboarding effectiveness.
• Use recruiting and hiring data to identify constraints, test solutions, and redirect resources toward the highest-priority markets and roles.
• Build external talent networks and internal pipelines for recurring, hard-to-fill, and leadership roles.
Leadership Development, Performance, and Capability Building
• Assess leadership and organizational capability needs and partner with Organizational Development, Learning, and business leaders to implement targeted solutions.
• Coach leaders on objective setting, performance differentiation, feedback, accountability, development planning, and career conversations.
• Build leader capability to coach and grow talent, make high-quality talent decisions, lead inclusively, and manage change.
• Identify systemic performance or capability gaps and sponsor interventions that strengthen execution and create measurable business impact.
Culture, Engagement, Inclusion, and Retention
• Shape a culture aligned with company values, leadership behaviors, ethics, customer focus, and accountability.
• Analyze engagement, retention, recognition, mobility, and workforce trends; partner with leaders on focused actions that address root causes and improve the team member experience.
•  Guide recognition and retention strategies that reinforce performance, leadership behaviors, and business priorities.
Employee Relations, Risk, and Compliance
• Provide strategic oversight and consultation on complex or high-risk employee relations matters, applying sound judgment, consistency, confidentiality, and timely escalation.
• Coach leaders to address performance, conduct, attendance, and workplace concerns early and effectively; identify recurring themes and implement preventive solutions.
• Partner with Employee Relations, Legal, Compliance, and other subject-matter experts on investigations, corrective action, accommodations, policy interpretation, and employment-law requirements.
• Ensure compliant and consistent execution of company policies, programs, and required practices while balancing team member advocacy and business needs.
HR Program Integration and Partnership
• Connect enterprise centers of expertise and HR operations to regional priorities across compensation, benefits, talent acquisition, learning, organizational development, people analytics, and employee relations.
• Lead or sponsor regional and enterprise HR initiatives, ensuring effective communication, adoption, measurement, and continuous improvement.
• Provide timely, executive-ready updates on people priorities, risks, decisions, outcomes, and recommended actions.
• Maintain field visibility to understand operational realities, strengthen leader partnerships, and validate whether people strategies are producing intended outcomes.
Qualifications
• Demonstrated success as a strategic HR business partner supporting senior leaders in a complex, geographically dispersed, or multi-unit organization.
• Advanced business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect people strategies to operating results and customer outcomes.
• Deep capability in talent planning, succession planning, workforce planning, organization design, leadership development, change management, and talent acquisition strategy.
• Strong analytical skills and experience using workforce metrics and qualitative insights to diagnose issues, develop recommendations, and measure impact.
• Executive-level communication, facilitation, consulting, influencing, coaching, and stakeholder-management skills.
• Sound judgment in complex employee relations, employment-law, policy, ethics, and organizational-risk matters.
• Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, challenge constructively, and drive disciplined execution.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and HR information, reporting, and talent systems; ability to travel as business needs require.
Education and Experience
• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
• Seven or more years of progressive HR experience, including significant strategic HR business-partner and leadership responsibility; experience in retail, field operations, or another multi-site environment preferred.
• Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered.
Certifications
SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or comparable senior-level HR certification preferred.

Job Description
The Director of Governance and Risk will report to the CISO within Advance Auto Parts and will focus on the defining and deploying governance and risk management frameworks across Advance Auto Parts.
The Director of Governance and Risk will oversee cybersecurity policy, standards, procedures, compliance, ensuring the company adheres to relevant regulations, industry standards, and internal and 3rd party risk management. The ideal candidate will combine expertise in both cybersecurity and risk management disciplines and have exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills.

This position is 4 days in office, 1 day remote per week, based at our corporate headquarters in Raleigh, North Carolina (North Hills)
The key responsibilities of the role include:
- Develop a short term and long-term comprehensive Governance and Risk Management Strategy
- Develop, communicate, and implement enterprise-wide security policy, standards, procedures, and guidelines.
- Provide strategic guidance to the CISO for the representation of risks to the Board, Audit committee, and ERM
- Lead a team of cyber specialists, providing direction and supporting their development
- Conduct regular risk assessments, including PCI-DSS and SOX, and develop comprehensive risk management plans for various business units and projects
- Support Internal Audit with engagements requiring technology support.
- Vendor Risk Management (VRM): Oversee the VRM integration, including risk reviews, contract management, and ongoing monitoring to manage risks associated with third-party vendors and suppliers
- Support the identification, evaluation, and prioritization of cyber risks across the organization
- Oversee production, reporting and evolution of cyber risk metrics, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), scorecards, and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)
- Conduct risk analysis, providing insights on issues and direction on risk mitigation strategies
- Drive automation, analytics, and continuous improvement of processes
- Engage with a range of senior stakeholders across Lines of Defense to ensure appropriate oversight and reporting of cybersecurity risks and vulnerabilities

About Advance Auto Parts

Founded in Roanoke, VA in 1932, Advance Auto Parts is a leading automotive aftermarket retail parts provider that serves both professional installer and do-it-yourself Customers. As of July 13, 2019, Advance operated 4,912 stores and 150 Worldpac branches in the United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The Company also serves 1,250 independently owned CARQUEST branded stores across these locations in addition to Mexico, the Bahamas, Turks, and Caicos and the British Virgin Islands. The company has a workforce of over 70,000 knowledgeable and experienced Team Members who are proud to provide outstanding service to their Customers, Communities, and each other every day.

About Advance India Innovation Center (AIIC) :

We are continually innovating and seeking to elevate the Customer experience at each of our stores. For an organization of our size and reach, today, it has become more critical than ever, to identify synergies and build shared capabilities. The Advance India Innovation Center (AIIC), located in Hyderabad, is a step in this strategic direction that enables us to access a larger talent pool, unlock operational efficiencies and increase levels of collaboration.

Job Summary
The Sourcing Advisory Analyst supports the identification, tracking, and analysis of product cost opportunities across the merchandising organization. This role leverages data, analytics, market intelligence, and reporting tools to provide actionable insights that improve product profitability and support sourcing and category management strategies.
Working closely with Category Management, Finance, and Strategic Sourcing partners, the Advisory Analyst develops reporting solutions, maintains cost tracking repositories, and conducts analytical assessments of commodity, freight, currency, and vendor cost drivers. This role plays a key part in enabling data-driven decision making through fact-based analysis and continuous process improvement.

jobs.title: Hub Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description
The Hub Operations Lead is responsible for the day to day operations and workflow of all HUB functions to include execution of store Hub order fulfillment, Inventory control and all associated processes. Depending on the size and scope of the HUB operations, some HUB Operations Leads will lead 1 or more team members assigned to HUB operations.  These roles are HUB Inventory Specialist and HUB drivers.  The individual in this role should have good knowledge of store systems, basic parts knowledge, good interpersonal skills and prior experience leading other Team Members. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and requires the ability to network with nearby stores, Hubs, pdq and external suppliers for order fulfillment. The role owns responsibility for maintaining Hub company standards.  This position is full time. Position may require MVR certification, and should complete all training materials and attend all store meetings.

Primary Responsibilities
- Responsible for Hub operations and resolution of Hub orders and processes in a timely manner
- Responsible to provide direction, organize and delegate work and ensure execution related to leading HUB related Team members (Hub /Loop Drivers and Hub Inventory Specialist)
- Review Hub orders, pulling parts, stage product, finalize paperwork
- Interaction with internal and 3rd party Drivers on paperwork, instructions
- Engaging store to facility network to determine part sourcing and logistics solutions, work with ordering store for fulfillment options if unavailable in network
- Work with GM, DM and CSC support for proper inventory mix and levels
- Inventory accuracy and functions as it relates to the parts department and HUB inventory to include- Onhand accuracy of inventory, shrink results, Cycle Counts, Outages, Planograms, Maxi changes, Price Changes, Front & Face, Truck lead
- Manage and comply with all Hub records and all paperwork policies and procedures
- Urgently Communicate any risks or concerns regarding order fulfillment or shipments to the appropriate store leader(s)
- Lead stocking activities from replenishment orders, to include scanning in product and ensuring completion within 24 hours

Secondary Responsibilities
- Additional Inventory activities including Overstocks, Callbacks, Resets
- Safely deliver parts to customers as needed
- Assist with Front Room Inventory functions
- Assist with cores and defects
- Fixed Activities: Store Cleanliness including floors, bathrooms, facing, dusting, parking lot
- Assist as needed with MOD and other store related actions

Success Factors
- Friendly communication
- Ability to locate and stock parts
- Safety knowledge and skills
- Operating inventory systems and store equipment, including forklift, pallet jack and/or hand jack
- Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
- Ability to execute and train inventory systems and store equipment
- High attention to detail

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Hub Operations Manager
- Must be competent at oral and written communications and handle basic math computations.
- Should have prior retail experience, including basic merchandising and inventory management skills.
- Able to drive forklift, if certified and applicable, and use a hand truck and pallet jack.
- Should be well mannered, neat in appearance and possess the ability to meet and deal with the public in an unbiased manner.
- Previous work records should demonstrate stability and performance results.
- Scheduling factors necessitate that the individual should be able to come to work on short notice, and/or work flexible hours including nights and weekends.
- Immediately report to General Manager and/or District Manager any violation of company policy or procedure.

Prior Experience that Sets a Hub Operations Manager up for Success
Inventory management in a retail environment or logistics center of operations
Education
High school diploma or general education degree (GED)
Certificates, Licenses, Registrations
None
Physical Demands
The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Work Environment
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
